title: The kernel of a sheafified quotient is the subsheaf of sections locally in the image
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space and let $\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\varphi}\mathcal G$ be a morphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Form the presheaf $P$ by $P(V)=\mathcal G(V)/\varphi_V(\mathcal F(V))$ for each open $V\subseteq X$, and let $P^#$ be its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Let $q:\mathcal G\to P^#$ be the composite. Then $\ker q$ is the subsheaf whose sections are locally in the image of $\varphi$, and consequently $q$ is an epimorphism and $q\circ\varphi=0$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01AH (tag 01AH, modules.tex lines 204-243): colimits in modules are sheafified presheaf colimits; Sites, Theorem 00WB and Lemma 00WK give the local section/equality criterion used for the kernel.

proof.text: Let $\eta:P\to P^#$ be the sheafification map and write $p_V:\mathcal G(V)\to P(V)$ for the sectionwise quotient. The quotient maps commute with restriction, so $P$ is a presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $q_V=\eta_V\circ p_V$ defines the morphism $q$. Since $p_V\circ\varphi_V=0$ for every open $V$, one has $q\circ\varphi=0$. The underlying sheaf of sets of $P^#$ with $\eta$ is the ordinary sheafification, by lem-weil-pbc-module-sheafification-underlying-sets.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01AH (tag 01AH), proof and statement of parts (1)--(2), lines 204-243; the module sheafification is Modules on Sites, Lemma 03CY (tag 03CY).

proof.text: Apply the local-section/equality criterion to the opens site of $X$ (Sites, 00WB and 00WK), using the underlying-sheaf identification from Step 1. For $s\in\mathcal G(V)$, the equality $q_V(s)=0$ is the equality $\eta_V([s])=\eta_V(0)$ in $P^#(V)$, and therefore holds exactly when some open covering $V=\bigcup_iV_i$ satisfies $[s|_{V_i}]=0$ in $P(V_i)$. By the definition of the quotient, this is equivalent to the existence of sections $t_i\in\mathcal F(V_i)$ with $s|_{V_i}=\varphi_{V_i}(t_i)$.

source.place: Sites, Theorem 00WB (tag 00WB, theorem-plus), especially parts (2) and (4), and Lemma 00WK (tag 00WK, lemma-sections-sheafification); applied to the opens site.

proof.text: For each open $V$ let $I(V)$ be the set of sections of $\mathcal G(V)$ that are locally of the form $\varphi(t)$. Restriction preserves this property. Given two such sections, refine their two covers to a common cover; on each member the sum, difference, and multiplication by a section of $\mathcal O_X$ are again images under the corresponding linear map. Thus $I$ is a subsheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules of $\mathcal G$ (the sheaf condition is inherited from $\mathcal G$). Step 2 identifies $I(V)$ with $\ker(q_V)$ for every $V$, so $I=\ker q$ as sheaves of modules.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01AH (tag 01AH), together with the sectionwise sheaf-of-modules structure and the local criterion from Sites 00WB/00WK.

proof.text: The map $\varphi$ factors through $I$ because every section in its image is locally in the image. Finally, let $h,k:P^#\to\mathcal H$ be morphisms with $h q=k q$. For any section $u\in P^#(V)$, 00WB/00WK gives an open cover $V=\bigcup_iV_i$ and sections $a_i\in P(V_i)$ with $\eta(a_i)=u|_{V_i}$. Each $a_i$ is $p_{V_i}(g_i)$ for some $g_i\in\mathcal G(V_i)$, so $u|_{V_i}=q(g_i)$ and $h(u)|_{V_i}=k(u)|_{V_i}$. The sheaf axiom for $\mathcal H$ gives $h(u)=k(u)$; hence $q$ is an epimorphism. Together with Step 1 this proves all remaining assertions.
